buyer: Analysts covering a sector through earnings season
pain: Too many calls, too little time, raw transcripts are noise
v1: A curated post-earnings note across one sector
verdict: Good leverage and fit, but the category is exactly where funded incumbents and model providers are shipping.

why.distribution: Direct to 20-50 analysts she knows, sold as a personal or small-team seat.
why.demand: Analysts already pay for transcript tools, so a paid substitute exists - which is also the problem.
why.fmf: She knows what matters in a call and has the AI fluency to automate the first pass.
why.revenue_structure: Per-seat monthly subscription with ordinary churn.
why.defensibility: AlphaSense, Fiscal.ai and every frontier model ship this; her curation is the only differentiator and it does not compound.
why.leverage: One note serves every subscriber during earnings season.
why.time_to_revenue: Needs a full earnings season to demonstrate value: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: AI budgets are real, but so is the commoditisation of exactly this task.
why.ceiling: £500/mo x 35 seats = £210k, requiring 35 paying seats against funded incumbents.

ceiling_arithmetic: £500/mo x 35 seats = £210k gross less model and data costs ~£15k = £195k. 35 seats is plausible from her network in principle; incumbent competition is what makes it hard.
carries: Real leverage, a buyer she can reach directly, and a task she understands better than a generalist software team.
kills: Defensibility at 1. She owns nothing when AlphaSense or a model provider ships the same summary.
test: Run it free for one earnings season for five analysts, then quote £500/mo.
test_pass: Two convert and say it replaced something.
test_fail: They liked it but kept using their existing platform.
